slides.title: All three can host Pally like Telegram, but none is as open
points: Each has an official way for a bot to chat with users.
Each one limits Pally in a different way.
Order: LINE first, WeChat as a pilot, KakaoTalk later.

details.label: Where our users already are
details.body:
Pally users whose phone number comes from a country where each app is the main messenger. Today they reach Pally over iMessage, WhatsApp or Telegram, so this shows who is already here, not how many new users a channel would bring.

WeChatChina, Hong Kong155
LINEJapan, Indonesia, Thailand, Taiwan67
KakaoTalkSouth Korea26

Out of 5,836 users with a phone number: about 2.7%, 1.1% and 0.4%. For scale, the US alone is 3,043.

details.label: Two different things we could build
details.body:
OptionWhat it meansPally does this today on
Pally's own accountUsers message a Pally bot, like a contactTelegram, iMessage
The user's own accountPally reads and sends from the user's own chatsWhatsApp

This report is about the first. The second is covered on the "Own accounts" slide.

slides.title: LINE is the closest fit to Telegram
points: A bot account that works in 1:1 chats and groups, with typing dots.
Any company can sign up, including foreign ones.
The catch: messages Pally starts, or slow replies, cost money.

details.label: What it costs (Japan prices)
details.body:
Quick replies to a user are free. Anything else is counted per person it reaches, against a monthly plan.

PlanPer monthMessages included
Free¥0200
Light¥5,0005,000
Standard¥15,00030,000 + extra

A free reply only works for about a minute after the user writes. Pally often takes longer than that, so in practice most replies will be paid.

slides.title: WeChat now has an official way to put an agent in a personal chat
points: Tencent's ClawBot (March 2026) adds an AI agent as a WeChat contact.
One-to-one chats only; each user links it by scanning a QR code.
Still rolling out slowly, with reports of lost messages.

details.label: The two ways into WeChat
details.body:
ClawBot (recommended)Business account
Feels likeA personal contactA brand page you follow
Pally can message firstSeems so, unprovenOnly 5 messages in 48 hours after the user writes
CostFree todayUS$99 a year verification
MaturityEarly, limited rolloutEstablished

The business account limit breaks reminders and automations, so ClawBot is the better bet if it works.

details.label: Risks to check before building
details.body:
• It may only exist in the mainland China version of the app, not international WeChat.
  • Developers report messages that WeChat says were sent but never arrive (October 2026).
  • Tencent publishes example code for it, so the build itself is well documented.

slides.title: KakaoTalk is possible but the hardest fit
points: Pally must answer every message within 5 seconds.
The real answer gets one chance to arrive, within about a minute.
Anything after that, or anything Pally starts, is paid.

details.label: How a reply reaches the user
details.body:
MomentWhat happensCost
Within 5 secondsPally says "working on it"Free
Within about 1 minutePally sends the real answer, onceFree
Later, or Pally startsSent as a separate notificationPaid per message

The one-minute answer needs Kakao to approve the feature first.

details.label: Can a non-Korean company do it?
details.body: Yes, since August 2026: a foreign company with an international business ID (D-U-N-S number) can get a verified business channel. Pally has 26 users in Korea today.

slides.kicker: What has to change in Pally
slides.title: Pally's channel rules cannot describe these apps yet
points: Pally knows "can always message" or "can message for X hours", nothing else.
Pally does not know that some messages cost money.
Pally assumes one shared bot, not one per user.

details.label: Which app needs which change
details.body:
ChangeLINEWeChatKakaoTalk
Know a message costs moneyNeededNeeded
Limits beyond "X hours"Business account onlyNeeded
One bot per userNeeded
No group chatsAlready supportedAlready supported

These rules live in one file every channel fills in (CHANNEL_FACTS).

slides.title: Reading the user's own chats is a separate project
points: Ready-made connectors exist for LINE and KakaoTalk.
WeChat has none, and Tencent bans unofficial apps.
This fits the Matrix connector proposal from the same day.

slides.title: Three decisions
points: Which first: LINE (easy, smaller audience) or WeChat (bigger audience, riskier)?
Are we willing to pay for LINE messages Pally starts?
Start building LINE now?

details.label: What was not checked
details.body:
• Whether ClawBot works on international WeChat.
  • Whether ClawBot lets Pally message first.
  • KakaoTalk's paid notification prices.
  • LINE's exact free reply window today.
